purpose: Teach: オッサン/のら/てぇ/きき/フツー/おぉ/ムッ/ヘビー

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんを「オッサン」って呼んじゃダメよ
lines.en: Sho, you can't call your dad an 'old man' like that.
lines.style: Light correction, almost amused. Gentle but firm. The tone of a mother who's heard this before. Not scolding—just redirecting.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんがのら犬を保護されたって聞いたよ
lines.en: Mom, I heard Dad rescued a stray dog.
lines.style: Bright, eager to share news. Quick intake of breath before speaking. The excitement of a child bringing a fact to his mother. Looks for her reaction.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが「ちょてぇ」って関西弁で仰ったわよ
lines.en: Sho, your father said 'chotee' in Kansai dialect, you know.
lines.style: Wry, slightly knowing. Soft emphasis on the dialect word. Amusement underneath—she's in on the joke of his speech. Not quite conspiratorial, but close.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんに変化のききを尋ねたよ
lines.en: Mom, I asked Dad about how he could tell something had changed.
lines.style: Thoughtful, genuinely curious. Careful phrasing—he's trying to be precise about what he asked. Soft, observant tone. Not rushing to the answer.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんはフツーのお父さんに見えて頼もしいわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad looks like an ordinary father, but he's really dependable.
lines.style: Warm, reflective. Slight pause before 'dependable'—she's noticing it anew. Soft voice. The tone of someone realizing something about the person they live with.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、お父さんが「おぉ、寒い」って仰ってたよ
lines.en: Mom, Dad was saying 'Oh, it's cold,' earlier.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact, almost understated. The tone of reporting a simple observation. Small, genuine laugh underneath. Not mocking—just noting the ordinary thing his dad said.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんがムッとされた瞬間が分かるわよね
lines.en: Sho, you can tell the exact moment when your dad gets annoyed, can't you?
lines.style: Reflective, gentle realization in her voice. Acknowledging his perceptiveness without making a big deal of it. A quiet moment of recognition between them.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、宿題ヘビーで終わらない様、ペース配分しろってお父さん
lines.en: Mom, Dad said my homework pile is getting heavy, so I need to pace myself better.
lines.style: Earnest, repeating what he was told with mild acceptance. Not complaining—just relaying information. The dutiful tone of a child taking parental advice seriously.
